name: Peer connection identity and generation binding
canonical_problem: Peer connections, direct/indirect tokens, server-supplied addresses, and pending outgoing messages are managed across several dictionaries without one durable connection-generation object.
why_not_separate: Fixes that only reject direct PeerInit, only randomize tokens, or only add pending-queue caps can leave replacement/promotion/buffer paths inconsistent.
coherent_fix_shape: Introduce a per-peer-init context with generation id, target user, conn_type, expected address policy, direct/indirect token state, queued-message budget, and explicit primary/secondary transition rules.
risk_of_bad_combination: High: strict secondary-connection closing can break compatibility; strict address equality can break NAT/indirect flows; token hardening alone can create false confidence.
rev0006_decision: No strict admission; make U-176 the dynamic test anchor for this family after U-123.

name: Transfer lifecycle provenance and state binding
canonical_problem: Transfer state is keyed by mixtures of username, virtual path, token, and connection state; some peer status/control messages do not carry enough fields to be strongly bound by themselves.
why_not_separate: Rejecting duplicate tokens, hardening UploadDenied, and changing FileTransferInit attachment independently can create inconsistent queues or orphaned timers.
coherent_fix_shape: Add a transfer generation/provenance object, reserve active tokens per username, preserve existing active transfer on collision, and treat low-context status messages as advisory unless they match the active/queued generation.
risk_of_bad_combination: Medium/high: protocol messages lack token fields in some cases, so a fix that requires nonexistent fields is not implementable without protocol breakage.
rev0006_decision: U-123 becomes the next microrepro-to-end-to-end workup; U-158 and U-169 stay as supporting tests.

name: Allowed heavy-response and request-generation gating
canonical_problem: Heavy peer responses need cheap allowed-response checks before decompression/materialization, but response ids must be specific enough to avoid username-only or token-only confusion.
why_not_separate: A username-only AddAllowedResponse gate fixes unsolicited large UserInfoResponse in master but does not necessarily bind a response to the exact socket/address/generation or UI tab request.
coherent_fix_shape: Key allowed responses by message class plus request token/generation and expected peer context; remove gates deterministically on completion, error, timeout, or tab removal.
risk_of_bad_combination: Medium: too-strict gates can drop legitimate legacy responses; too-loose gates preserve spoofing/resource windows.
rev0006_decision: U-217 downgraded to upstream-partially-fixed/residual; parser-ordering family remains queued for a later deep pass.

name: Server-supplied address policy
canonical_problem: Server-mediated peer address data can feed connection attempts before local address-class policy and pending-request budgets are applied.
why_not_separate: Address validation interacts with ConnectToPeer, GetPeerAddress, direct/indirect fallback, and socket caps.
coherent_fix_shape: Add reserved-address policy and per-request budget as a local safety layer, with compatibility escape hatches where protocol behavior requires it.
risk_of_bad_combination: High: hard equality or hard reserved-address refusal can break unusual but legitimate network configurations.
rev0006_decision: Keep as backlog design item; not the next report candidate.
